summary: Survey of elite panic, the pattern of owners and authorities endangering people during disasters out of fear of the public, from the 2004 Ycuá Bolaños fire in Paraguay to the 1906 San Francisco and 1964 Alaska earthquakes.

evidence.note: Paiva's rise from butcher to supermarket owner opens the episode
son orders exits barred so no one leaves without paying while the store burns
2006 verdicts, riots and later retrial with longer sentences
segment on studies showing wealth reduces empathy and raises entitlement
host states the true subject is the phenomenon of elite panic, coined by sociologists
1906 San Francisco earthquake and fire segment begins
Funston imposes martial law; mayor authorizes troops to shoot looters
officials and media spread false Katrina violence rumors, delaying rescues
brief move to de Blasio and early Covid as a present-day example
Alaska earthquake: police deputize drunk volunteers and halt survivor search

notes: Primary subject is a concept; movement-or-ideology is the closest kind. Transcript dates the Alaska quake to March 1962 (magnitude 9.2); it was 1964, used here. Origin US = where the term was coined. Paiva's birth year not given, so floruit 2004. Covered span ends at the Paraguay retrial (2008); Katrina 2005 and Covid 2020 are short instances, the latter setting reaches_present. PY ranked first as the centrepiece harm though US airtime is similar.
